No. The method did not detect any tree-cover loss event of 0.5 ha or more on ASSET-D (311.2 ha) between 2021-01-01 and 2025-12-31. Hansen Global Forest Change (GFC-2025-v1.13) had valid observations over 100% of the property, and its series runs through 2025. The JRC 2020 map shows 285.6 ha of forest (91.77% of the property) at the baseline, so there was substantial tree cover that could have been lost.

This is not proof that nothing changed. Losses under 0.5 ha, losses at edges, and losses narrower than the 30 m pixels may be missed. The result is also not a regulatory or compliance finding, such as EUDR or deforestation-free status. It says nothing about periods outside 2021–2025.

The evidence is current as of 2026-11-12. One source, MGAP 2021, was unavailable.
